definitions.explanation: A type of persimmon that loses its astringency on the tree and can be eaten raw when ripe, as opposed to the astringent {渋柿|しぶがき}.

examples.japanese: {甘柿|あまがき}は{生|なま}で{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: Sweet persimmons can be eaten raw.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{木|き}に{甘柿|あまがき}がなった。
examples.english: Sweet persimmons grew on the tree in the garden.

examples.japanese: {甘柿|あまがき}は{渋柿|しぶがき}と{違|ちが}い、{熟|じゅく}すと{自然|しぜん}に{甘|あま}くなる。
examples.english: Unlike astringent persimmons, sweet persimmons become sweet naturally as they ripen.

notes:
A persimmon variety that is sweet enough to eat raw once ripe. Contrasted with the astringent {渋柿|しぶがき}, which must have its astringency removed before eating.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘柿|あまがき}の{品種|ひんしゅ}: varieties of sweet persimmon
- {甘柿|あまがき}をもぐ: to pick sweet persimmons

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {渋柿|しぶがき}: astringent persimmon — inedible raw until de-astringed or dried
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}: dried persimmon — usually made from {渋柿|しぶがき}
